newsitem.title: UK: Pharmaceutical stocks lifted by weaker sterling.
newsitem.headline: Pharmaceutical stocks lifted by weaker sterling.

text.p: Shares in Britain's leading pharmaceutical stocks advanced on Thursday, helped by a weaker currency and persistent bid rumours.
Shares in SmithKline Beecham Plc hit a 12 month high after adding 13-1/2p to 857p by 0845 GMT. Glaxo Wellcome Plc gained 7-1/2p to 931-1/2p and Zeneca Group was up 13-1/2p to 857p.
"The opening prices reflect the depreciation in sterling," said one trader. "It has lifted the exporters."
Sterling's recent strength has seen it peak at its highest levels since dropping out of the ERM in September 1992.
"Together with the bid rumours, the fall in sterling has really helped the sector," said the trader.
Long-standing rumours that Swiss drugs giant Roche Holding may be looking to merge with a foreign drugs company resurfaced on Wednesday, leading to sharp gains in British pharmaceutical stocks.
Analysts described the merger rumours as "pure speculation" stemming from talk that Roche may be poised to sell off its fragrances business.
